trust_decision.summary: The HTTP/1.1 request-header parser decides whether a request has reached max_headers, but it counts distinct map keys (maps:size) rather than header lines, so duplicate names are folded into one key by comma/'; ' concatenation and never count against the limit.

landing_point.why: The only place max_headers is read in the repo for HTTP/1.1; the maps:size(Headers) comparison is the obvious culprit given the 'duplicate header names' summary.

fix_sites.entry_point: Any HTTP/1.1 request on a cowboy:start_clear/start_tls listener (cowboy_http protocol)
Same: header line completion in HTTP/1.1 request parsing (counter increment)
Same: resumption of header parsing after a partial TCP read ({more,...} state)
Same: start of header block after request line
Same: counter threaded through name/value parsing and saved in every {more,...} / error state

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The only non-obvious part is the resume-from-partial-read path (src/cowboy_http.erl:406-413, 682, 737): a solver who counts lines in a local variable but does not persist it in #ps_header{} would reset the count on every TCP segment; a solver could argue 'the test request arrives in one packet'. No genuine second route exists in this repo.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Duplicate header lines must still be accepted and combined (', ' join, '; ' for cookie) up to the limit; 99 duplicate lines plus Host must still return 200. An over-broad fix rejecting duplicate names outright breaks RFC7230 3.2.2 combining.

O6_input_shapes: repeated non-cookie header name (values joined with ', ')
header block split across multiple TCP reads (count must survive the {more,...} resume state)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Trailer parsing is a 4096-byte binary:split stub; a planted 'proper trailers' parser that reuses the header map and maps:size would be a direct sibling.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The code carries '%% @todo Proper trailers.' (src/cowboy_http.erl:1084); a maintainer implementing it would naturally copy parse_header's map-based logic.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A resume clause that rebuilds #ps_header{} without carrying the line count (count reset per TCP segment).
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The fix had to add num_headers to every state save; missing one save is a plausible maintainer slip and is a HOW-type sibling (state crossing a partial-read boundary).

O9_family: CWE-770 resource exhaustion: per-request header-count limit bypass via duplicate-name folding

O10_build.toolchain: Erlang/OTP 24+ with erlang.mk (make) or rebar3; deps cowlib and ranch fetched from git
O10_build.project_tests: Common Test suite test/rfc7230_SUITE.erl limit_headers/1 (test/rfc7230_SUITE.erl:1042) and combine_duplicate_headers/1 (test/rfc7230_SUITE.erl:1022)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Count lines in a local accumulator inside parse_header/parse_hd_value without persisting it in #ps_header{}, or reject any duplicate header name.

out_of_scope_notes: HTTP/2 max_headers (src/cowboy_http2.erl:58) is enforced inside cowlib's cow_http2_machine, which is not in this tree.
HTTP/3 opts declare no max_headers at all (src/cowboy_http3.erl:30-53); header decoding lives in cowlib's cow_http3_machine, not in this repo, and HTTP/3 is experimental (COWBOY_QUICER).
unverified: repo_mb not measured; Cowboy's src/ is about 30 Erlang modules, so tiny_repo (<5 MB source) is an estimate, not a measurement.
Whether cowlib's HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 header decoders count duplicate fields correctly was not checked (cowlib is not in the pinned tree and is out of repository scope).
single_site is not flagged: the fix touches several functions, but they all carry one counter for one check in one file; in spirit this host is single-concept.
